appraisal_events.evidence: Jupien ne m'avait pas plu beaucoup au premier abord...il résultait de ce désaccord entre son regard et sa parole quelque chose de faux qui n'était pas sympathique.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's first impression of Jupien is unfavorable: a mismatch between his sorrowful eyes and his cold, mocking speech reads as something false and unlikeable.

appraisal_events.evidence: je discernai vite en effet chez lui une intelligence rare et l'une des plus naturellement littéraires qu'il m'ait été donné de connaître...Il avait de la bonté, de la pitié, les sentiments les plus délicats, les plus généreux.
appraisal_events.explanation: That initial impression is overturned as the narrator discovers Jupien's rare natural intelligence, literary gift, and deep kindness and generosity, ranking him among the most gifted people he has known.

appraisal_events.evidence: Françoise n'avait pas encore compris que les plus cruels de nos adversaires ne sont pas ceux qui nous contredisent et essayent de nous persuader, mais ceux qui grossissent ou inventent les nouvelles qui peuvent nous désoler...pour notre complet supplice, à la fois atroce et triomphant.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Françoise's naivety in treating the gossiping valet de chambre as a friend, when his exaggerated, alarming reports actually make him one of the household's more damaging adversaries.

status_effects.explanation: His first appearance strikes the narrator as false and unappealing.
A separate, later moment of discovery strongly reverses that first impression, revealing rare intelligence and generosity.
Her severe homesickness ('ennui') in the new household is quickly relieved thanks to Jupien's friendship.
Her judgment is shown to be naive: she mistakes a damaging gossip for a friend.

ambiguities: The valet de chambre who misleads Françoise is unnamed and not on the reference sheet, so the diminishment in E3 is scored against Françoise's misjudgment rather than against him as a character.
